people.name: Sen. Ted Cruz
people.niche: US senator (R-TX), chair of Senate Commerce; light-touch AI regulation and federal preemption
people.reason: As Commerce chair he writes the Senate's main AI agenda (the SANDBOX Act, the state-law moratorium push) and is the leading congressional voice for AI deregulation framed as a race with China.
people.gap: Without him the map lacks the elected free-market, anti-'Big Government–Big Tech' deregulatory view that treats existential-risk talk as hype and state AI laws as a patchwork to override.

people.name: Sen. Marsha Blackburn
people.niche: US senator (R-TN), kids' online safety, creators' likeness rights (NO FAKES), TRUMP AMERICA AI Act
people.reason: She led the 99-1 vote to strip the state AI-law moratorium and argues for the protections she calls the '4 Cs' (children, creators, conservatives, communities), a populist-right case for regulating AI.
people.gap: Without her the map has no right-of-centre voice for duty-of-care rules, likeness and copyright protection for artists, and a federal floor rather than a ceiling, which splits the right against Cruz-style preemption.
people.flag: Her official site (blackburn.senate.gov) returns HTTP 403 to plain requests, so two of her five works are verbatim mirrors of her office's press releases on capitolreleases.com; the owner may prefer to swap these for the originals.

people.name: Steve Bannon
people.niche: Host of War Room, national-populist strategist; anti-Big-Tech, anti-transhumanist
people.reason: He is the loudest MAGA-populist voice against AI accelerationism and tech 'oligarchs', and he publicly backed Blackburn's AI framework.
people.gap: The map lacks the national-populist, anti-tech-elite strand of the right without him.
people.flag: NOT SOURCED: no work met the standard in this pass. I found no op-ed or essay by him on AI, and War Room is video or audio with no speaker-labelled text transcripts I could verify. The session's web-search budget ran out before a deeper search. Recommend a later pass that looks for a written piece or a speaker-labelled transcript.

people.name: Tucker Carlson
people.niche: Independent media host (Tucker Carlson Network); AI-sceptic populist commentary
people.reason: His interviews and monologues reach a very large audience with deep scepticism of AI, of tech leaders' motives, and of AI's effect on work and meaning.
people.gap: The map lacks the populist-media sceptic voice that treats AI as a spiritual and civilisational threat without him.
people.flag: NOT SOURCED: no work met the standard in this pass. tuckercarlson.com sits behind a Cloudflare challenge, so it is not fetchable as plain text. I found no op-ed by him on AI, and I could not verify a speaker-labelled transcript (for example of his 2025 Sam Altman interview) before the session's web-search budget ran out. Recommend a later pass.

people.name: Michael Kratsios
people.niche: Director, White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP); architect of the 2025 AI Action Plan
people.reason: He is the administration's chief AI policy voice at home and abroad: 'AI dominance', export of the 'American AI stack', and outright rejection of global AI governance.
people.gap: Without him the map lacks the official US executive-branch accelerationist and sovereigntist position that calls 'so-called existential risk' and safety-focused forums obstacles to progress.
people.flag: Industry ties: he was a managing director at Scale AI between his two OSTP terms, and earlier chief of staff at Thiel Capital. Worth noting for the owner, though not a conflict with Anthropic.

people.name: Gov. Ron DeSantis
people.niche: Governor of Florida (R); state AI Bill of Rights and data-centre limits
people.reason: He is the most prominent Republican executive defying federal preemption, pairing child-safety and consumer rules with a moral, religious critique of AI 'supplanting' humans.
people.gap: Without him the map lacks the states'-rights conservative who opposes both Big Tech and a federal block on state AI laws, with concern for jobs, utility bills and 'online slop'.
people.flag: Only 3 usable works. His AI statements are mostly at press conferences (video only), and a further search was cut short by the session's search budget.

works.author: ted-cruz
works.title: Will AI's Future Be American?
works.channel: RealClearWorld (reproduced in full by the Senate Commerce Committee)
works.note: About 700 words. Positions: the US must beat China so AI reflects American rather than authoritarian values; government should enable AI, not inhibit it; the SANDBOX Act offers two-year waivers from outdated rules; state AI-specific laws are duplicative because existing law already covers AI. The committee page adds a short press-release intro; the op-ed text is his alone.

works.author: ted-cruz
works.title: Sen. Cruz: AI Policy Should Harness the Power of American Ingenuity (opening statement, 'AI've Got a Plan' hearing)
works.note: Remarks as prepared, about 650-700 words. Lays out his five-pillar AI framework: permitting for AI infrastructure, countering foreign censorship, preventing a state patchwork, stopping AI-enabled fraud against seniors, protecting human dignity. Introduces the SANDBOX Act ('Conduct that is illegal without AI will remain illegal with AI'). Use the /press/rep/release/ URL; the /2025/9/ variant returns 403.

works.author: ted-cruz
works.title: Sen. Cruz: Adopting Europe's Approach on Regulation Will Cause China to Win the AI Race (opening statement, 'Winning the AI Race' hearing)
works.note: Remarks as prepared, about 850-900 words. Attacks EU 'command-and-control' rules and the Biden AI executive order (audits, risk assessments, anti-discrimination testing); praises rescinding the AI Diffusion Rule; previews a bill to stop 'needless' state over-regulation; 'The country that leads in AI will shape the 21st century global order.' Hearing witnesses included Sam Altman.

works.author: ted-cruz
works.title: Sen. Cruz: Congress Should Not Allow a Big Govt-Big Tech Takeover of AI (executive session opening statement)
works.note: Remarks as prepared, about 850-900 words, of which roughly half is on AI (the rest covers unrelated bills). Positions: AI law should be incremental and targeted; broad rules invite regulatory capture by incumbents; existential-risk claims are overhyped by companies; regulation pushes innovation to China. Supports the TAKE IT DOWN Act on deepfakes and concedes cyber risks may need action now. The earlier work in the set (from when he was ranking member).

works.author: ted-cruz
works.title: 'We Must Do Both:' Commerce Chairman Ted Cruz Talks AI Acceleration, Risk Management at Axios and Politico Summits
works.channel: US Senate Commerce Committee (transcript excerpts of Axios and Politico interviews)
works.note: About 550 words, mostly quoted blocks of Cruz's own words from two live interviews, with committee framing text around them. Covers the 1990s-internet light-touch model vs EU prior approval, a Chinese win meaning AI as a tool of surveillance, deepfake takedown, and kids: no social media under 13, no algorithmic boosting under 17. 'AI is coming whether you like it or not.' Caveat: these are excerpts chosen by his committee staff, and interviewers' questions are mostly not shown.

works.author: marsha-blackburn
works.title: On AI, Congress just provided a huge win for children, creators and conservatives
works.note: About 550-600 words, signed 'By Sen. Marsha Blackburn'. Defends her amendment striking the 10-year state AI-law moratorium (passed 99-1); names harms (copyright, voice and likeness theft, AI child sexual abuse material); says states such as Tennessee (ELVIS Act) must keep acting until Congress passes preemptive laws (KOSA, NO FAKES, a privacy framework). Likely syndicated to other Tennessee papers.

works.author: marsha-blackburn
works.title: Opening statement, 'The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly: AI-Generated Deepfakes in 2025' (Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on Privacy, Technology, and the Law)
works.channel: US Senate Judiciary Committee (GovInfo hearing record)
works.note: Official, speaker-labelled hearing record ('OPENING STATEMENT OF HON. MARSHA BLACKBURN'; 'Chair Blackburn'). Her opening is about 600-650 words; the full transcript also has her questioning. Positions: AI is beneficial in logistics, health and music (Randy Travis), but deepfakes 'cause tremendous harm' to creators, children and fraud victims; push to pass NO FAKES this year; rising AI child sexual abuse material. Extract only the passages labelled as hers.

works.author: marsha-blackburn
works.title: Keynote with Senator Marsha Blackburn, State of the Net 2025
works.channel: State of the Net conference (Internet Education Foundation), transcript PDF via ISOC Live
works.note: 6-page monologue transcript labelled 'Sen. Marsha Blackburn (R-TN):'. The AI section is about a third of it: AI can do 'tremendous good' but bad actors exploit it; DeepSeek toes the Chinese Communist Party line; AI threatens artists' voice and likeness; calls for a national preemptive online privacy law. The rest covers KOSA, cybersecurity and China (Salt Typhoon), quantum and spectrum. Text-layer PDF, extractable.

works.author: marsha-blackburn
works.title: Blackburn to CNBC: Big Tech's Opposition Must Not Stand in the Way of Federal Legislation to Govern the Virtual Space
works.channel: Office of Sen. Blackburn press release (mirror on Capitol Releases; original blackburn.senate.gov returns 403)
works.note: About 600 words, mostly her quoted answers from the CNBC AI Summit in Nashville. Positions: federal preemption, because states act only when Congress fails; regulate AI by use, not technology; a federal privacy law to control AI training on personal data; consent for name, image and likeness; chatbots' effects on children; KOSA. A short framing summary attributed to CNBC's Ian Thomas is not hers. Original URL: https://www.blackburn.senate.gov/2025/10/technology/blackburn-to-cnbc-big-tech-s-opposition-must-not-stand-in-the-way-of-federal-legislation-to-govern-the-virtual-space

works.author: marsha-blackburn
works.title: Blackburn Unveils National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence (TRUMP AMERICA AI Act)
works.channel: Office of Sen. Blackburn press release (mirror on Capitol Releases; original blackburn.senate.gov returns 403)
works.note: About 900 words: her statement plus the release's summary of the framework. Positions: one federal AI rulebook replacing the state patchwork; a duty of care to prevent foreseeable harm; child-safety duties for chatbots; a private right to sue over data and likeness used in training or replicas; political-viewpoint bias audits for high-risk systems; reporting on AI job losses; data centres pay their own energy and water costs. Caveat: it includes endorsement quotes from Mike Davis and Steve Bannon, and the framework summary is office text, so attribute to her only her quoted statement and the framework positions. Original URL: https://www.blackburn.senate.gov/index.php/2025/12/technology/blackburn-unveils-national-policy-framework-for-artificial-intelligence

works.author: michael-kratsios
works.title: Statement on 'Advancing America's AI Action Plan' before the House Science Subcommittee on Research and Technology
works.channel: US House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology
works.note: Written testimony PDF, about 800 words. Positions: the three Action Plan pillars (innovation, infrastructure, international partnerships); moving 'from strategy to execution'; innovators need 'regulatory clarity and certainty' from Congress; relieving 'undue regulatory burdens'; shielding US firms from 'foreign nations' stifling regulatory regimes'; the American AI Exports Program.

works.author: michael-kratsios
works.title: Testimony, 'AI've Got a Plan: America's AI Action Plan' (Senate Commerce Subcommittee on Science, Manufacturing, and Competitiveness)
works.channel: US Senate Commerce Committee (GovInfo hearing record)
works.note: Official, speaker-labelled record. His opening statement is about 1,500 words, and his labelled Q&A answers total about 6,500 words. Positions: 'global dominance in AI'; the gap with China was closing by 2024; approach AI 'not with fear, but with responsible boldness'; the tech-stack export strategy; regulatory relief. The same record holds Cruz's statement (not used here; his prepared text is listed separately). Extract only the passages labelled 'Mr. Kratsios.'

works.author: michael-kratsios
works.title: Remarks by Director Kratsios at the APEC Digital and AI Ministerial Meeting
works.note: As prepared, about 1,300 words, Incheon, Korea. Positions: speed AI innovation, infrastructure and 'AI diplomacy'; a full-stack American AI Exports Program for allies; support for open-source and open-weight models as a sovereignty tool; overregulation (Europe) leaves countries behind; 'human judgment and friendly cooperation' over 'global governance and technocratic control'.

works.author: michael-kratsios
works.title: US statement at the Security Council open debate 'Artificial intelligence and international peace and security' (10005th meeting)
works.note: The most-cited statement of the US position: 'We totally reject all efforts by international bodies to assert centralized control in global governance of AI'; 'Ideological fixations on social equity, climate catastrophism and so-called existential risk are dangers to progress'; broad overregulation 'incentivizes centralization' and risks tyranny. Caveat: UN Transcripts is an automatic speech-recognition transcript with speaker identification; the page holds the whole meeting (44 speeches), so isolate the US segment, and quote anchors may contain ASR errors. Prefer the official verbatim record S/PV.10005 when it becomes available.

works.author: michael-kratsios
works.title: Remarks by Director Michael Kratsios at the India AI Impact Summit
works.note: About 1,600 words, New Delhi. Positions: 'We totally reject global governance of AI'; sovereignty means adopting the American AI stack, since 'complete technological self-containment is unrealistic'; a safety focus on 'speculative risks' entrenches incumbents and spreads 'an atmosphere of fear'; does back trust-building rules on child protection and intellectual property. Announces the National Champions Initiative, the AI Agent Standards Initiative and the Tech Prosperity Corps.

works.author: ron-desantis
works.title: 2026 State of the State Address (as printed in the Journal of the Florida Senate)
works.channel: Journal of the Florida Senate, 2026 bound volume I (joint session record)
works.note: Full address text is printed in the journal, about pp. 7-8 of the 8 MB PDF. The AI passage is about 350 words: AI 'threatens to upend key parts of our economy' and leave many out of work; consumers foot the bill for data centres; 'real perils for children', with chatbots linked to teen suicides; 'online slop'; whoever controls data inputs can make 'truth an elusive concept'; technology must be 'moral and ethical'; 'We welcome technologies that enhance the human experience, but not those purporting to supplant it', citing Ecclesiastes and humans 'made in the image of God'. The rest of the speech is not about AI.

works.author: ron-desantis
works.title: Governor Ron DeSantis Announces Proposal for Citizen Bill of Rights for Artificial Intelligence
works.channel: Executive Office of the Governor of Florida press release (mirror via Public Technologies, published unedited)
works.note: About 600 words: his quoted statement (about 70 words) plus the office's itemised proposal. Positions: an AI Bill of Rights (data privacy, parental access to children's chatbot conversations, consent for name, image and likeness, chatbot disclosure, no AI 'licensed' therapy, a ban on DeepSeek and Chinese AI in government, AI not the sole basis for insurance claim denials); data centres: no ratepayer or taxpayer subsidies, local power to ban them, water protection, no foreign owners. The flgov.com original was not reachable at the expected URL (404); the mirror states it is unedited.

works.author: ron-desantis
works.title: Governor Ron DeSantis Signs Law to Protect Floridians from Subsidizing Data Centers
works.channel: Executive Office of the Governor of Florida
works.note: Short (about 350 words): his quoted statement (about 80 words) plus a summary of SB 484. Positions: local governments keep authority to reject hyperscale data centres; costs, including electricity, are not passed to residential and small-business customers; protect water resources; no utility service to data centres controlled by foreign countries of concern. Narrow (data centres only) but shows the policy enacted.
